blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Sustainability, at the senior level, is no longer a reporting requirement — it is a strategic variable that reshapes the supply chain the same way cost, service and risk do. The companies that treat it as an afterthought are slowly finding that their biggest customers, their biggest investors and their biggest regulators are asking questions that will eventually change the cost of doing business in ways the finance function cannot ignore.

The strategic questions are not soft. Which products, which lanes, which suppliers carry the heaviest footprint, and what would it cost — in money and in time — to redesign them? Where can we get a real advantage from being earlier and more honest than competitors? Which changes will be forced on us anyway in five years, and would we be better off making them on our own schedule instead of theirs?

Sustainability as strategy is not about saving the planet in a press release. It is about accepting that the rules of the game are changing, positioning the company for where they are going, and making the changes deliberately — because the companies that wait will, eventually, be forced to make the same changes in a crisis, at a worse price, by people who did not ask for their consent.

items.q: According to the text, at senior level sustainability is best understood as…
options: a matter for the finance function alone
a strategic variable that reshapes the supply chain
items.why: "it is a strategic variable that reshapes the supply chain the same way cost, service and risk do."

items.q: Why can the finance function no longer ignore sustainability?
options: Because customers, investors and regulators are asking questions that will change the cost of doing business
Because it is a purely reputational concern
Because reporting standards have become simpler
Because competitors have already stopped investing
items.why: "their biggest customers, their biggest investors and their biggest regulators are asking questions that will eventually change the cost of doing business."

items.q: The phrase "The strategic questions are not soft" most likely implies that…
options: the questions concern only public relations
the questions are hard, concrete and financially consequential
the questions are optional and can be deferred
the questions are gentle and easy to answer
items.why: Inferência: "not soft" contrasta com as perguntas difíceis sobre footprint, custo e cronograma — são decisões duras, não retórica.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Some changes will be imposed regardless of what the company does.
Sustainability is essentially a press-release exercise.
Acting early can create a genuine competitive advantage.
Waiting to act may mean changing under worse conditions later.
items.why: Inferência: o texto afirma explicitamente que a sustentabilidade "is not about saving the planet in a press release".

items.q: The final sentence suggests that companies which delay will…
options: end up changing anyway, but at a worse price and on someone else's terms
items.why: Inferência: "forced to make the same changes in a crisis, at a worse price, by people who did not ask for their consent."

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte encerrar o programa de estratégia de sustentabilidade. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Two years ago, in this same room, I opened this programme by asking a single question: not whether we can afford to invest in sustainability, but whether we can afford not to. I want to close by returning to it.

Over these two years we have stopped treating this as a reporting exercise and started treating it as what it actually is — a strategic variable, sitting alongside cost, service and risk. We have mapped the footprint of every major lane, we have redesigned the three worst offenders, and we have built the traceability that our largest customers are now, frankly, demanding as a condition of the contract.

Let me be blunt about what we have learned. What we measure, we manage. What we manage, we improve. And what we improve, we sustain. Reporting without action is greenwashing; action without measurement is guesswork. We have tried very hard to do neither.

So I leave you with the question I opened with. If not us, who? If not now, when? The rules of this industry are changing whether we consent or not. My recommendation is simple: let us keep making these changes on our own schedule, deliberately — rather than in a crisis, at a worse price, on somebody else's terms.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What question did Charlotte use to OPEN the programme two years ago?
options: How much the finance function would allow
Whether the company had the right suppliers
Not whether they can afford to invest, but whether they can afford not to
items.why: "not whether we can afford to invest in sustainability, but whether we can afford not to."

items.q: According to Charlotte, what concrete progress has the programme delivered?
options: It cut headcount and consolidated offices
It outsourced measurement to a third party
It produced a new sustainability report only
It mapped the footprint of every major lane, redesigned the three worst offenders and built traceability
items.why: "we have mapped the footprint of every major lane, we have redesigned the three worst offenders, and we have built the traceability."

items.q: How does Charlotte distinguish greenwashing from guesswork?
options: Reporting without action is greenwashing; action without measurement is guesswork
Greenwashing is a regulatory term; guesswork is a financial one
Both mean the same thing in practice
Measurement without reporting is greenwashing; action without cost is guesswork
items.why: "Reporting without action is greenwashing; action without measurement is guesswork."

items.q: Why does Charlotte return to her opening question at the end?
options: To rhetorically frame the talk as complete and hand the decision back to the team
To correct something she said earlier
Because she has run out of new material
To ask for a budget increase
items.why: Inferência: o "circle back" fecha o discurso e devolve a decisão à liderança — recurso retórico, não repetição por falta de conteúdo.

items.q: What is the underlying message of "the rules of this industry are changing whether we consent or not"?
options: Change is optional for market leaders
Regulators will not act for at least a decade
External pressure is inevitable, so it is wiser to act deliberately and early
The company can veto external change
items.why: Inferência: se a mudança é inevitável, a escolha real é entre agir no próprio cronograma ou ser forçado depois — o argumento central de Charlotte.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "For years the board treated emissions as an afterthought, tacked onto the annual report." An afterthought is…
options: something considered late and given little weight
items.why: Afterthought = consideração secundária, algo pensado por último e sem prioridade.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Air freight on that lane carries by far the heaviest carbon ___, so we moved it to sea."
items.why: Footprint = pegada (de carbono), o impacto ambiental atribuído àquela operação.

items.q: "We would rather make these changes on our own schedule than have them imposed in a crisis." Here schedule means…
items.why: Schedule = cronograma; aqui, o ritmo/tempo escolhido pela própria empresa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Being earlier and more honest than rivals is not virtue for its own sake — it is a competitive ___."
items.why: Advantage = vantagem: posicionar-se antes dos concorrentes gera diferencial competitivo.

items.q: "Real change is deliberate; a glossy press release without action is greenwashing." A press release is…
options: an official public statement to the media
items.why: Press release = comunicado à imprensa; sem ação por trás, vira greenwashing.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de estratégia e sustentabilidade. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The audit committee still has to sign off on the traceability standard before we publish it." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the new sourcing policy region by region over the next year." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two suppliers pushed back on the emissions clause, arguing it was unworkable." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The board endorsed the targets but never followed through on the funding." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A single certified lane will not move the needle on our overall footprint." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = fazer diferença perceptível; aqui, não move o indicador de forma relevante.
